catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class posts a transfer session addressed by deck position IDs. cap.fluid.transfer.v1 requires well-level source and target objects and returns transferred volumes, while this client takes deck position IDs and returns a session id and status, so the exact interface is an extension.
catalogue_requests.summary: Post one source-to-destination transfer and create a transfer session.

catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class starts a previously posted transfer session by session id; the catalogue has no session-lifecycle class.
catalogue_requests.summary: Start the transfer session with the given id.

catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue read class reads the status of a named transfer session. cap.sensing.read.v1 binds sensor resource kinds only and has no session-id input, so the status read is an extension with an inline schema.
catalogue_requests.summary: Read the status of the transfer session with the given id.

catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class cancels a named transfer session. cap.motion.stop.v1 is a motion stop and takes no session id; the client's only stop path is cancel_transfer_session(session_id).
catalogue_requests.summary: Cancel the transfer session with the given id.

catalogue_requests.reason: The R2 hardware driver needs a no-input safe-state action, and no catalogue class cancels the active transfer session without input. The action cancels the session the driver last created or started; with no tracked session it queries the instrument status.
catalogue_requests.summary: Cancel the active transfer session (the safe state).

notes:
DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card names the python-object family, but this is a direct Driver because the upstream post_transfer_session takes a list of TransferParameters dataclasses and the driver holds the session id for the stop path. Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored (deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017, run wB2-103) and unreviewed: reviewed_by is null, the R2 hardware backend is refused until a human signs, and nothing here is a hardware run or a human review. The hardware path (native.py and a real instrument URL) was never run; the fake is an in-memory object, not a recording. The transfer volume is Limit.operator_required: no text file of the clone states a volume range or the tip capacity of a unit, so every transfer is refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET until the site supplies the range; site-limits.example.json is an example overlay, not a device bound. NOT COVERED: posting a deck layout (post_deck_layout), because the clone does not document the GET deck document and a writable state field cannot carry the LabwarePosition list without inventing that schema; the deck layout is read-only. NOT COVERED: the optional TransferParameters fields aspiration_speed, dispense_speed, air_gap, touch_off, mix_cycles, mix_volume, blow_out and retract_distance, because no text file gives their ranges. The client has no global stop request: the e-stop cancels the session the driver last created or started, or queries the instrument status when none is tracked, and cancel_active_transfer does the same. No independent hardware e-stop is documented in the clone, so estop_physical_ref is not set. gate.digest is the digest line the check printed; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
